headline: Learn to build AI systems that still work when real people use them.
tagline: A hands-on course for engineers and new graduates. Start with how a model works, then prompt engineering, build RAG from a 50-line script to a service, then learn agents, LangChain, evals, deployment, voice, fine-tuning, MLflow, Kubeflow, model serving and llama.cpp. Every hard word is explained.

howTo.title: Read, then run.
howTo.text: Most lessons have code in the code folder. Open a terminal beside the page and run it. Each lesson says what was run and what was only read.

howTo.title: Go in order the first time.
howTo.text: Each lesson fixes a problem the last one left. Skipping ahead makes the fixes look random.

howTo.title: Answer the check questions out loud.
howTo.text: If you cannot explain it to a teammate, read that part again.

howTo.title: Look up any hard word.
howTo.text: The glossary explains every term in one or two lines, and search works across all lessons.

howTo.title: Want to go further?
howTo.text: The Dig deeper track holds our source notes: what we read, what each source teaches, and what we could not verify.

ladder.title: A script that answers from your documents
ladder.text: 50 lines, no database, no framework. You see the whole idea before any tools get in the way.

ladder.title: Cleaner input and smarter chunks
ladder.text: Most bad answers start with bad text going in. Fix the reading and cutting first.

ladder.title: Search that finds the right piece
ladder.text: Keyword search, vector search, and mixing both. Then reranking and rewriting the question.

ladder.title: Answers you can trust
ladder.text: Prompts that stay inside your documents, point to sources, and say 'I don't know' when they should.

ladder.title: Measure before you tune
ladder.text: A test set and a few numbers, so every change is a fact and not a feeling.

ladder.title: Fast, cheap, and safe
ladder.text: Caching, cost control, access rules, and keeping private data private.

ladder.title: Running it for real
ladder.text: A web service, logs, monitoring, updates when documents change, and a launch checklist.

tracks.title: Foundations
tracks.blurb: What a language model does, what tokens and context windows are, your first API call, writing prompts, and getting JSON back. Five short lessons.

tracks.title: Prompt engineering
tracks.blurb: How to ask a model so it answers well. Zero-, one- and few-shot examples, chain of thought, roles and context, ReAct, retrieval-augmented prompting, self-consistency, tree of thought, and guardrails. Nine lessons.

tracks.title: RAG: from POC to production
tracks.blurb: Make an AI answer from your own documents. Fourteen lessons take you from a 50-line script to a service you can launch, then seven more cover upgrades: reranking, rewriting, other ways to chunk, vectors at scale, judging answers, agentic search and graphs.

tracks.title: Case study: RAGFlow
tracks.blurb: Open a real open-source RAG product and map it onto the RAG track: how it reads PDFs, cuts and embeds, searches, cites, runs agents, and what it leaves out. Read from the code, four lessons.

tracks.title: Agents and LangChain
tracks.blurb: Agents, LangChain, LangGraph, deep agents, managed deep agents, OpenWiki, and how to find integrations. Four lessons, one runnable graph.

tracks.title: Harness engineering
tracks.blurb: Everything around the model that makes an agent usable: the loop, tools, permissions, memory, logs. DeepSeek Harness is the worked example.

tracks.title: Evals and observability
tracks.blurb: Datasets, experiments, judges, live checks, refining prompts, and tools like LangSmith Engine that find problems for you.

tracks.title: Deploy and monitor
tracks.blurb: Tracing, dashboards, alerts, where to host an agent, the LLM gateway, and a script that watches upstream docs for changes.

tracks.title: Voice AI
tracks.blurb: How an AI phone or web call works: the speech-to-text, model, text-to-speech chain, where the delay hides, turn-taking, WebRTC, SIP and LiveKit.

tracks.title: LiveKit, self-hosted
tracks.blurb: LiveKit from the wire to production, run on your own machines. WebRTC and SFUs, the lk CLI, rooms, tokens, the server API, webhooks, media and data, the Agents framework, turn-taking, tools and workflows, local models, frontends, testing, SIP telephony, recording, ingress, deployment and scaling. Twenty-eight lessons and a Docker lab where every script was run.

tracks.title: Voice in production
tracks.blurb: The case study that follows the LiveKit track: a real phone-agent platform and the engineering that keeps calls alive. Phone audio, carrier adapters, auth on sockets, async hot paths, events, retries, latency, privacy, testing, shipping, and a production checklist. Fourteen lessons.

tracks.title: Pipecat and Dograh
tracks.blurb: Learn Pipecat coming from LiveKit, then read Dograh, an open-source voice agent platform built on a fork of it: the frame model, interruptions, turns, the graph that becomes tool calls, the visual builder and its live view, what the fork changed, and a study plan to your first pull request. Nineteen lessons, with runnable demos.

tracks.title: LLMOps and fine-tuning
tracks.blurb: When to prompt, retrieve, or fine-tune. Training data, SFT, LoRA, DPO, tracking runs, scoring answers, and watching a live system.

tracks.title: MLflow
tracks.blurb: Track runs, save models with their schema, register versions with aliases, serve over HTTP, trace and evaluate LLM apps, version prompts, and run a shared server safely. MLflow 3.18, eight lessons, most of them run.

tracks.title: Kubeflow
tracks.blurb: What Kubeflow is in 2026 (and what is deprecated), a KFP pipeline run with no cluster, standalone Pipelines on kind and where it failed for us, Trainer, tuning, KServe and the two MLflow bridges. Five lessons, with honest notes on what was not run.

tracks.title: Inference and edge
tracks.blurb: What a model server does with your prompt: prefill, decode, KV cache, vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Dynamo, GGUF, and fair benchmarks.

tracks.title: llama.cpp, end to end
tracks.blurb: Run models on your own hardware and understand the engine underneath. Clone and build, GGUF files, training a tiny model and taking it through convert, quantize, run and serve, sampling, llama-server, an AI engineer's playbook, benchmarks, then the internals: a map of the code, ggml tensors and backends, inside libllama, your own C++ program, and contributing. Fourteen lessons, built and run at a pinned commit.

tracks.title: Dig deeper: research notes
tracks.blurb: The source notes behind the lessons: what each outside resource teaches, how to read it, and what we could not verify. Start here if you want to go further.
